articles.title: A California recycling business operating on leased land since 2017 faced eviction after Metro bought the property for a light rail project; a November 24 appeals court let Metro's possession case proceed
articles.summary: A scrap metal recycling business in Van Nuys, California, could face eviction from premises it had occupied for years after the property's acquisition by
articles.body: A scrap metal recycling business in Van Nuys, California, could face eviction from premises it had occupied for years after the property's acquisition by a public transport agency for a light rail project. The business owners challenged the eviction proceedings, arguing that the agency had to follow eminent domain procedures rather than pursue a separate unlawful detainer case. However, on November 24, 2026, the California Court of Appeal denied their petition, allowing the possession case to proceed.In its published decision in Zavala Family Inc. v. Superior Court, B352255, available on Justia, the California Court of Appeal, Second Appellate District, Division Eight, examined whether the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) could seek possession through an unlawful detainer action after purchasing the leased property for public use. The court concluded that the acquisition had terminated the existing lease and the tenants' possessory interest, rejecting their principal arguments against the eviction proceedings.Recycling business had operated on the property since 2017According to the court's November 24 decision, Zavala Family Inc. and Jose Zavala had operated a scrap metal recycling business on a parcel in Van Nuys since at least April 2017. They leased the premises from the trustees of the Etzel Trust. In September 2023, Metro notified the occupants of its intention to acquire the property for the East San Fernando Valley Light Rail Transit Project. The notice also informed them of their potential eligibility for relocation benefits under the federal Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970.Metro subsequently informed the occupants in February 2024 that it had made an offer to purchase the property. Both notices stated that the occupants would receive at least 90 days' written notice before being required to move. In June 2024, the Etzel Trust entered into an agreement to sell the property to Metro. The agency obtained ownership through a grant deed recorded on January 23, 2025.Metro then sent the business operators three notices asking them to vacate, dated February 21, March 14 and May 14, 2025. However, they continued occupying the premises.On October 6, 2025, Metro filed an unlawful detainer action seeking immediate possession. The agency argued that its acquisition of the property for public use had automatically terminated the existing lease under California Code of Civil Procedure section 1265.110. Since the occupants had not entered into a new agreement with Metro, the agency considered them holdover tenants without a continuing leasehold interest. Three days later, Metro also filed an eminent domain action seeking to acquire improvements located on the premises for the light rail project.Business owners challenged Metro's eviction proceedingsThe business operators challenged the unlawful detainer complaint, arguing that the trial court lacked jurisdiction because the eminent domain proceedings gave the condemnation court exclusive authority to determine possession of the property. They also maintained that section 1265.110 only released tenants from their obligation to pay rent after a public acquisition and did not automatically extinguish their right to occupy the premises.Additionally, they argued that Metro had to follow section 1255.410 of the Eminent Domain Law to obtain possession. That provision establishes procedures for public entities seeking possession before a final judgment in an eminent domain case, including requirements involving compensation deposits, notice and the consideration of hardship.The Los Angeles County Superior Court overruled their demurrer, allowing Metro's unlawful detainer case to proceed. The business operators then petitioned the Court of Appeal for a writ of mandate, asking it to overturn the trial court's decision and direct it to dismiss the eviction complaint.Appeals court explains why Metro could pursue possessionThe Court of Appeal rejected the business operators' arguments against the use of an unlawful detainer action in this particular case. First, it explained that section 1230.050 gives an eminent domain court authority to determine possession of the property involved in the condemnation proceedings. However, that authority does not prevent a public entity from pursuing other lawful methods of acquiring property, including purchasing it through an agreement with its owner.The court noted that Metro had acquired the property through a purchase from the Etzel Trust rather than through a completed eminent domain proceeding. Therefore, the exclusive jurisdiction provision did not automatically prevent the agency from pursuing possession through an unlawful detainer action. Second, the court disagreed with the argument that section 1265.110 only terminated the tenants' rental obligations. It explained that when an entire property subject to a lease is acquired for public use, the lease terminates, ending both the landlord-tenant relationship and the tenant's possessory interest, unless the lease contains a valid provision establishing different rights.The court also clarified that the former occupants could have negotiated a new lease with Metro, but no such agreement had been reached. Regarding the protections under section 1255.410, the court explained that these procedures apply when a public entity seeks possession after filing an eminent domain lawsuit but before establishing its entitlement to acquire the property. Metro, however, had already purchased the premises and obtained title before filing its unlawful detainer complaint.Consequently, the court concluded that the prejudgment possession procedures did not prevent Metro from pursuing the separate possession case. The court also discussed California's Relocation Assistance Act, which generally requires at least 90 days' written notice before a person lawfully occupying property is required to move a business because of a public project. However, the business operators had not raised a deficient-notice argument in their demurrer or appellate briefs. The court therefore did not decide whether Metro's three successive 30-day notices satisfied the applicable 90-day notice requirement.Court denies petition and allows case to proceedThe Court of Appeal denied the petition for a writ of mandate, concluding that the arguments presented by the business operators did not justify overturning the trial court's decision. It also vacated its earlier temporary stay of the unlawful detainer proceedings and awarded costs to Metro.The ruling does not itself constitute a final eviction order or establish that the business has already been removed. Rather, it allows Metro's possession case to continue in the lower court. The Court of Appeal also clarified that its decision was limited to the arguments raised by the business operators and did not establish that unlawful detainer would always be an appropriate method of determining a tenant's possessory rights after a public acquisition.You use AI every day. articles.title: Reform UK pledges to scrap graduate visa route, calls it a ‘scam’ allowing low-skilled migrants to remain in Britain
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent from London: Nigel Farage’s party, Reform UK, has pledged to scrap graduate visas if they are voted into govt, claiming they are a
articles.body: TOI Correspondent from London: Nigel Farage’s party, Reform UK, has pledged to scrap graduate visas if they are voted into govt, claiming they are a “scam” being used as a back door for low-skilled migrants to remain in Britain.“It enables foreign nationals who are not studying and have no job to stay in Britain by the back door. A staggering 600,000 have been dished out in the last three years, 70% of which have gone to Indian, Pakistani and Nigerian nationals. Thousands of them go on to overstay and claim asylum. We would end it immediately,” said Reform shadow home secretary Zia Yusuf.According to home office statistics, in the year to June 2026, 5,130 people who had held graduate visas claimed asylum.The route allows international students who have completed a UK degree to remain in the UK for two years to work or look for work without any minimum salary requirement.Instead, Reform plans to give international students 30 days after finishing their studies to secure a job that “meets a strict economic contribution test”.Reform’s shadow education secretary, Suella Braverman, wrote in the Daily Telegraph that she had fought to scrap the route as home secretary but had been blocked by then PM Rishi Sunak. She wrote that students converting to graduate visas were “far from the brightest and best”.“A home office study found just one in four went to a Russell Group university and only 65% were employed full-time. It has become a back door to Britain for low-skilled migrants to cheat the system,” she wrote.Indian nationals were granted the highest number of graduate visas in the year ending Sept 2026.Reform, which is polling level with the Conservatives in second place, behind Labour, has also pledged to scrap indefinite leave to remain and replace it with a renewable five-year visa that requires migrants to demonstrate a significant economic contribution.Indian National Students Association president Amit Tiwari said: “Reform’s targeting of international students, particularly Indians, is deeply disappointing: their fees help keep UK universities afloat, their spending supports local economies, and their research strengthens Britain.”You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Think twice': Banff officials issue warning over thin ice after skater's death
articles.summary: After three separate incidents, one fatal, at Lake Louise, Parks Canada is warning visitors to be cautious after a warmer than average November.
articles.body:
A 70-year-old local resident of Banff, Alberta, has died after falling through ice on Lake Louise, prompting warnings about outdoor safety as Canada experiences warmer than normal November temperatures.

Police said the man, who has not been identified, was ice skating alone on Tuesday evening when he fell through thin ice. He was found two hours later by a rescue team and pronounced dead at a nearby hospital.

It comes after two other ice skaters fell in the lake's frigid waters on Monday, though both survived.

Canadian park authorities have issued a warning to visitors of the world-famous Banff National Park urging them to "think twice" before stepping on the ice.

"Visitors must be able to self-rescue should they fall in the water," Parks Canada said in a notice posted on Monday.

"If you choose to skate on natural ice, you do so at your own risk."

In a statement, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police offered condolences to the 70-year-old's family. It also warned the public of the dangers of being on the ice.

Parks Canada said that early season ice can be unpredictable, and that it does not actively monitor natural ice surfaces for safety or mark potential hasards.

The incident comes as temperatures in Alberta and other parts of Canada have been warmer than average for this time of year.

Canada's largest city, Toronto, experienced unseasonable highs of 15C (59F) this month.

In Alberta, temperatures have been about three degrees Celsius warmer than what has been historically observed for November, Alysa Pederson, a meteorologist with Environment Canada, told the BBC.

On average, temperatures would dip below -10C for a number of days in November. But this year, Pederson noted that the coldest November day was -6C.

"It's going to become a challenge to form ice when your temperatures aren't really getting that cold," Pederson said.

Environment Canada's seasonal forecast suggests that much of Canada , from Vancouver to Halifax, will likely be seeing a warmer than average winter.

It is due partly to the weather phenomenon known as El Niño, where changing wind patterns over the Pacific Ocean result in heat being released into the atmosphere that can drive major shifts in global weather patterns.

"We're currently in a very strong El Niño event, potentially record-breaking by the time it peaks here in the next couple of months," Pederson explained.

She advised those who are eager to get outside in the winter to stay vigilant, as warmer weather can not only mean thin ice, but a higher risk of avalanches.

She added that while falling through ice in Banff is always a risk, the recent back-to-back incidents came as a surprise and called it "unfortunate".

articles.title: Texas marching band raises $350,000 for two extra hotel nights to keep 500 stranded students in New York after Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed due to storm
articles.summary: A Texas high school marching band has raised $350,000 to cover the unexpected costs of keeping its 500-member group in New York after the Macy’s
articles.body: A Texas high school marching band has raised $350,000 to cover the unexpected costs of keeping its 500-member group in New York after the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed until Saturday due to a potentially historic storm forecast for the region.The Pride of Pearland Marching Band from Pearland High School had travelled to New York for the annual parade, but the schedule change meant the students and staff needed additional hotel accommodation, meals and transportation. The fundraising effort received support from local businesses and people who contributed after the band's appeal spread on social media."It's been exhausting and emotional to figure this out, but it has been incredibly humbling to see an outpouring of kindness," Ryan Demkovich, director of the band, told CBS News.Demkovich said the community had responded to an urgent appeal to ensure the students could remain in New York and perform in the parade."This was quite a challenge for us, and there was a very frantic and large call to action to our community to let the kids stay here and finish it out," he added.How the band raised $350,000 after the parade delayThe donations helped the Pride of Pearland Marching Band cover two additional nights of hotel accommodation, extra meals and charter buses for the journey back to Texas after Saturday's parade.The group also faced a change in its accommodation arrangements. The Marriott Marquis in Times Square, where the band had been staying, was booked for the weekend, so the students and staff had to relocate to a hotel near the Meadowlands Sports Complex in New Jersey.With flights fully booked until late Monday or Tuesday, the band decided to travel home by bus after its performance on Saturday.The fundraising campaign gained momentum through social media, attracting contributions from Pearland businesses as well as people who had no direct connection to the school. Texas businesses including Gringo's Mexican Kitchen in Pearland, Houston's Mattress Mack and CenterPoint Energy were among those that contributed through the fundraising link on the band's website.Other marching bands also seek help with extra expensesThe Pride of Pearland Marching Band was not the only group facing unexpected costs after the parade postponement. Eight other marching bands are scheduled to perform on Saturday, and some also appealed to their communities for financial support.The Dobyns-Bennett High School Band from Kingsport, Tennessee, asked for donations to cover the additional expenses of remaining in New York. In a social media post, the group said the delay had created unplanned costs, including extra hotel nights, extended charter bus rentals and meal allowances for students.The band also noted that the performance was particularly significant because it coincided with its own centennial year and the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.By Thursday morning, the Dobyns-Bennett Band announced that it had reached its fundraising goal, although it did not disclose the amount. The group confirmed that it had secured the money needed for an additional night in New York and an extended bus contract to take the students home on Saturday.Parade postponement disrupts plans for families and visitorsThe schedule change also affected tourists and relatives who had travelled to New York to watch the parade on Thursday. The Sims family, who had come from Florida to see their daughter perform with the Great American Marching Band, were among those left reconsidering their travel plans."We came up to see her. It's our first time in New York City," Dustin Sims told CBS New York. "We've had a great week, but now we gotta decide whether we're gonna stay another day or not."For the students in the marching bands, the postponement meant more than an unexpected change to their travel arrangements. Performing in the parade is a rare opportunity to reach millions of spectators along the route and watching from home, making the fundraising efforts crucial to ensuring they could still take part.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Oregon family took over a mobile home abandoned for five years for free, then spent about $14,000 restoring it so a mother and her twin daughters could move in and celebrate Thanksgiving under their own roof
articles.summary: An Oregon family has turned an abandoned mobile home into a comfortable place to live, giving a mother and her two teenage daughters a home of their own
articles.body: An Oregon family has turned an abandoned mobile home into a comfortable place to live, giving a mother and her two teenage daughters a home of their own just in time for Thanksgiving. Lyman Branson II, his parents and other relatives spent months repairing a property that had been empty for five years. Their aim was to provide a safe and stable home for Lyman's sister, Betty Branson, and her 17-year-old twin daughters. The family worked together to complete the project and give them a place to celebrate the holiday. The Bransons got the abandoned 1977 mobile home for free in the small town of Irrigon. But although they did not have to pay for the property, the work needed to make it liveable was extensive.A dilapidated shell ready for the dumpAccording to Realtor.com, Lyman Branson described the property as "basically... ready for the dump" when the family first saw it. Years of neglect had left the inside badly damaged. The floors and walls were rotting, water had caused serious damage and there were large holes in the ceiling. Despite its condition, Lyman believed the home could be saved. He had more than 20 years of experience maintaining and renovating rental properties, which helped him recognise that the structure was still worth repairing. He also saw the project as an opportunity to help his sister and her daughters find a secure place to live.Turning sweat equity into a homeThe renovation brought several challenges, particularly as the cost of materials and unexpected repairs began to rise. The family had initially expected to spend between $10,000 and $12,000, but the final bill reached about $14,000 after costs increased and they chose to improve some of the finishes. According to Realtor.com, the final amount was still far below the $20,000 Betty had been paying in rent each year. The family also received help from viewers of Lyman's YouTube channel, "I Can Fix That". They contributed an estimated $1,000 to $2,000 towards the cost of materials. Betty, 42, also played an active role in the work. She put in her own time and effort, working alongside her brother and father after finishing her regular job. She admitted that she initially felt "overwhelmed and kind of scared", but continued with the project because she knew having a home of her own would make a lasting difference to her family.From rubble to new beginningsThe months of work paid off in the first week of May 2026, when Betty and her daughters received their certificate of occupancy. This came just two weeks before the permits and a rent-free agreement with the landowner were due to expire. The family had transformed the nearly 50-year-old mobile home into a modern property that met current building codes. The work included installing new insulation, drywall and flooring, making the building suitable for the family to move into. The renovation also gave Betty and her daughters a chance to make decisions about their own living space. After renting for nearly two decades, they could finally choose how they wanted their home to look and feel. For Lyman and Betty's mother, LeAnna Branson, seeing the project completed brought relief and happiness. "It gave us a peace of mind to know... that she finally has a place of her own to call her home," she told Realtor.com.One of the most personal parts of the renovation was left behind the new cupboards. The family wrote their names and left messages of love on the walls before the cupboards were fitted. The notes remain hidden from view, serving as a lasting reminder of the effort and care that went into building the home. This Thanksgiving, the Bransons will gather in Irrigon to celebrate the holiday together. For Betty and her daughters, the occasion will also mark their first holiday season in a home made possible by the work of their family.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Supreme Court raps MNCs for ‘double standard’ on food quality
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday called out the “double standard” of multinational companies in producing foodstuff for Indian consumers inferior
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday called out the “double standard” of multinational companies in producing foodstuff for Indian consumers inferior in quality to what they did in Western countries, saying it was “deeply troubling”.While directing FSSAI to enforce front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) to make consumers aware of the contents of packaged food, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran deliberated on the dual yardsticks MNCs follow.“Concerns have been raised that certain multinational FBOs operating in India adopt practices towards Indian consumers that differ from those they follow elsewhere, including in the composition of their products and in the information provided on their labels. Such companies comply with, and in some instances voluntarily adopt, FoPNL requirements in other jurisdictions, yet resist similar measures here. If true, such double standards are deeply troubling,” the bench said.Saying a consumer in India was entitled to “no less protection and no less information” than one in the US or UK, SC said, “We would urge such multinational FBOs to adopt uniform standards across jurisdictions, and to extend to Indian consumers the same regard and respect for their health that they extend to consumers elsewhere.”It also directed FSSAI to ensure FBOs do not conceal or alter the composition of their products, or add additives, artificial preservatives, emulsifiers, etc, to soften the effect of FoPNL. “The introduction of a warning label must not become an occasion for reformulation that is hidden from the consumer, or that places the consumer at comparable or greater risk,” SC said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Quoting former US President Theodore Roosevelt to say justice consisted not in being neutral between right and wrong, but in finding out the right and upholding it, the Supreme Court Thursday quashed Bihar’s decision to allow the premature release of former MP and strongman Anand Mohan in the 1994 lynching case of district magistrate G Krishnaiah.The state government had amended prison rules to pave the way for Mohan’s release by removing the provision that disqualifies a person from remission if he is convicted of a public servant’s murder. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the amendment, saying it was indefensible and no rationale was given for changing the law. It directed Mohan to surrender within a month.“The notification dated April 10, 2023, is declared unconstitutional, invalid and inoperative, and is hereby set aside. The order dated April 24, 2023, granting premature release to (Mohan), is hereby quashed,” the bench said.The court said the state government could initiate a fresh procedure to amend the remission policy. “It is clarified that any future process to revise or amend Rule 481 shall not be initiated prior to (Mohan) surrendering within a month or being taken into custody, as the case may be,” it said.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
